newsitem.title: USA: Jason sees 1997 as "much stronger" year.
newsitem.headline: Jason sees 1997 as "much stronger" year.

text.p: Jason Inc, which reported lower 1996 fourth quarter and year-end earnings as expected, said Monday it believes 1997 will show improvement.

"We are disappointed that the difficulties this year in the Power Generation market were sufficient to prevent another new earnings record, but are pleased that our growth in the other segments offset most of the Power Generation shorfall," said Vincent Martin, chairman and chief executive.
"We believe 1997 will be a much stronger year," he said in a statement.

Earlier today, Jason reported 1996 fourth quarter earnings fell to $1.2 million or $0.05 a share from $3.2 million or $0.16 in the same period a year ago. Full year earnings declined to $8.9 million or $0.43 from $11.5 million or $0.56 in 1995. Jason had previously forecast a decline in earnings.
Earnings declined in the company's Power Generation segment due to a continuing weak market in the United States as well as lower margins on several international projects. Sales for
the 1996 fourth quarter increased to $121.0 million from $95.1 million a year earlier. Sales for the full 1996 year rose to $443.4 million from $407.4 million in 1995.
